premises.text: Mass retail cannot offer niche prestige makeup colors because supply-chain volume constraints limit assortment
premises.evidence_span: Walmart can't offer you all the colors that expensive prestige stores can, like Sephora. Why? Supply chain

premises.text: A desktop makeup printer turns any image/hex color into wearable cosmetics using inkjet-like substrates and FDA-compliant ink
premises.evidence_span: Mink is a desktop printer that prints makeup. It can take any image and instantly transform it into a wearable color cosmetic

premises.text: No new software is required; users pick a hex code and print as with an ordinary inkjet
premises.evidence_span: You do not need any new software. All you need is a color picker to copy the hex code and any software to print

premises.text: Hardware retails around $300 with commodity-priced ink and substrates; initial target is girls ages 13–21
premises.evidence_span: I'm going to retail this for about $300 initially. And the ink and the substrates are going to be commodity priced

premises.text: Platform expands beyond eyeshadow to lipsticks, powders, creams, foundations, with a developer ecosystem
premises.evidence_span: We're printing eyeshadow right now, but this is basically gonna be able to print lipsticks, powders, creams, foundations

value.text: Give consumers prestige-level color selection with mass-level / at-home convenience by printing makeup from the web
value.evidence_span: It gives you the selection of prestige and it combines it with the convenience of mass

secondary_value.text: Let girls control the definition of beauty rather than corporations
secondary_value.evidence_span: The definition of beauty is something that they should be able to control, not our corporations

causal_links.evidence_span: if you want like the cool niche colors, you have to go to expensive Sephora
turning any phone, laptop, or camera into an endless beauty aisle
change how the world buys makeup

notes: Founder bio excluded. Price and target segment packaged in P4 per commercial atomicity. Cosmetic format expansion listed as roadmap module P5.
